About Shomaji & Associates

Shomaji & Associates

Legal Practitioners and Consultants
Trial Advocacy & Litigation Excellence Since 1986

Full-Service Law Practice Based in Dhaka

Shomaji & Associates is a full-service law firm based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Since 1986, experience in criminal litigation, civil disputes, company disputes, and corporate matters. It is a leading law firm specialized in trial advocacy under the leadership of Ehsanul Haque Shomaji. The Firm’s principal areas of practice encompass international crimes, corruption, money laundering and financial crime, homicide and other serious criminal offences, cybercrime, corporate and commercial criminal litigation, narcotics-related offences, offences involving arms and explosives, including offences under the general and special laws, family matters, and civil matters. The Firm has been engaged in complex and high-profile criminal proceedings, including matters of substantial legal and jurisprudential significance. Its practice is distinguished by a commitment to rigorous legal research, principled advocacy, strategic case preparation, and the effective representation of clients before the competent courts and tribunals throughout Bangladesh.

Chamber Practice Focus

Our Practice Areas

Delivering high-caliber legal counsel and courtroom representation across diverse legal areas in Bangladesh.

Criminal Law

Supreme Court Chamber & High Court Litigation Division

Premier criminal litigation chamber providing specialized trial advocacy, pre-trial advisory, statutory defense, and appellate representation before trial courts, Special Judge Courts, Druto Bichar Tribunals, and the Supreme Court of Bangladesh since 1986.

Detailed Practice Information

Civil Litigation

Original, Revisional, Appellate & Review Jurisdiction

Shomaji & Associates provides strategic trial and appellate representation in complex land and property disputes, title and possession, partition, contractual specific performance, money suits, eviction, and civil appeals under the laws of Bangladesh.

Detailed Practice Information

Corporate Law

Corporate Governance, Financial Crimes, Banking Recovery & Commercial Arbitration

Comprehensive legal representation in financial crimes, Negotiable Instruments (NI Act Sec 138), Artha Rin Adalat, corporate governance, commercial arbitration, M&A restructuring, and banking credit disputes.

Detailed Practice Information

Family Matter

Matrimonial Disputes, Child Custody & Shariah Advisory

Compassionate and rigorous advocacy in marriage, divorce, dower (denmohor), maintenance, child custody, guardianship, dowry defense, and Muslim family law.

Detailed Practice Information

Terms & Conditions

Legal notice and usage terms of Shomaji & Associates

1. General Disclaimer

The materials and information contained on this website are provided for informational and educational purposes only, in accordance with the regulations of the Bangladesh Bar Council. They do not constitute formal legal advice or the establishment of a lawyer-client relationship until a formal vakalatnama or engagement agreement is executed.

2. Confidentiality

Shomaji & Associates treats all initial inquiries and consultation requests with the highest standards of professional secrecy and advocate-client privilege recognized under the Evidence Act 1872.

3. Intellectual Property

All articles, case analyses, branding logos, and content published on this website are the intellectual property of Shomaji & Associates and may not be reproduced without explicit written consent.

Privacy Policy

How Shomaji & Associates protects client data and confidentiality

1. Information Collection

When you submit a consultation request or contact message, we collect your name, phone number, email, and brief case details solely for the purpose of communicating with you and assessing your legal matter.

2. Non-Disclosure & Security

Shomaji & Associates does not sell, rent, or disclose personal client data to third parties. All consultation requests are stored securely on our dedicated servers and handled strictly by our authorized advocates and staff.

3. Contact & Rights

You may request the deletion or update of your inquiry records at any time by contacting us directly at info@shomaji.com.

1. Associate

Qualified learned advocates may apply to become associates at Shomaji & Associates by making an application to the Head of Chambers. The application should be accompanied by a current CV of the applicant. Interested candidates are requested to contact the chamber for an appointment.

2. Intern

Fresh law graduates may apply for a week-long internship at Shomaji & Associates by making an application to the Head of Chambers. The application should be accompanied by a current CV of the applicant.

Home / Practice Areas / Criminal Law
Chamber Practice Focus & Trial Advocacy

Criminal Law

Supreme Court Chamber & High Court Litigation Division

Criminal Law & Jurisprudential Scope

Premier criminal litigation chamber providing specialized trial advocacy, pre-trial advisory, statutory defense, and appellate representation before trial courts, Special Judge Courts, Druto Bichar Tribunals, and the Supreme Court of Bangladesh since 1986.

Governing Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed principally by the International Crimes (Tribunals) Act 1973, Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2004, Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012, Cyber Security Ordinance 2025, Narcotics Control Act 2018, Arms Act 1878, Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000, Special Powers Act 1974, Penal Code 1860, and Code of Criminal Procedure 1898.

Chamber Disciplines & Areas of Practice (12)

Comprehensive advisory, statutory frameworks, and courtroom litigation representation across specialized criminal law areas.

01.

International Crimes Practice (ICT-BD) (International Crimes)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, legal consultation and specialised legal research in matters arising under international criminal law, including proceedings before the International Crimes Tribunal of Bangladesh and the relevant appellate forums, subject to the scope of engagement and applicable law. The practice encompasses complex legal issues concerning crimes against humanity, genocide, war crimes and other offences falling within the jurisdiction of the competent tribunal.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is grounded in the International Crimes (Tribunals) Act, 1973, the International Crimes Tribunal Rules of Procedure, and other applicable laws of Bangladesh. Depending on the issues arising in a particular matter, relevant international legal sources may include the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, 1998, the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and their applicable Additional Protocols, customary international law, international humanitarian law, and the jurisprudence of domestic and international courts and tribunals. The relevance and legal effect of each source are assessed in accordance with the applicable law, the jurisdiction of the forum and the circumstances of the proceedings.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: The firm’s services include legal representation before the competent forums, professional legal consultation, conduct of trial proceedings and advanced legal research on substantive, procedural and evidentiary questions arising in international criminal proceedings. Research and case preparation may involve analysing indictments, charge-framing orders, investigation materials, witness statements, documentary evidence, judicial precedents and relevant international legal authorities. Depending on the engagement, the firm may also undertake the preparation of legal opinions, case analyses, written submissions and research memoranda, together with legal work relating to trial proceedings, appellate challenges and other remedies available under the applicable law. All work is undertaken with a focus on rigorous legal analysis, accurate interpretation of the governing legal framework, careful assessment of the evidentiary record and observance of the applicable procedural safeguards.

02.

Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Related Practice (Financial Crimes & ACC)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in proceedings involving allegations of corruption, illicit enrichment, abuse of public office, embezzlement and financial misconduct under the laws of Bangladesh. The practice encompasses criminal litigation before the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) and Special Judge Courts.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, the Penal Code, 1860, and other applicable legislation governing corruption-related offences, investigation, prosecution and trial.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our litigation approach is grounded in a rigorous assessment of the statutory ingredients of each alleged offence, the prosecution’s evidentiary foundation, and the legal basis for attributing criminal liability to each accused. We examine the complaint, FIR, investigation reports, charge sheet, witness statements, documentary evidence, financial records and relevant expert materials to identify evidentiary gaps, inconsistencies, questions of admissibility and deficiencies in the proof of essential elements. Particular attention is given to allegations involving acquisition of assets disproportionate to known sources of income, illicit enrichment, abuse of public office, misappropriation of funds, financial transactions and alleged conspiracy or complicity. Depending on the facts and applicable law, our analysis may address the source and ownership of assets, the distinction between suspicion and legally sufficient proof, the individual role and state of mind of each accused, and whether the evidence establishes the necessary connection between the accused and the alleged offence.

03.

Murder and Serious Offences (Homicide & Serious Crimes)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation and litigation services in criminal proceedings involving allegations of murder, culpable homicide, attempted murder, kidnapping, grievous bodily harm, robbery, dacoity and other serious offences under the laws of Bangladesh. Subject to appointment and engagement in individual matters, the firm represents accused persons and other clients entitled to legal representation at investigation, pre-trial, trial, sentencing, appellate and revision stages before the competent courts.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Penal Code, 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the Evidence Act, 1872, and applicable special legislation. It includes proceedings under relevant provisions concerning homicide, offences against the person, robbery, dacoity, criminal breach of trust and other serious crimes.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: The firm undertakes fact-specific legal analysis of the alleged offence, the prosecution's evidentiary case, individual criminal responsibility, applicable statutory defences and legally sustainable grounds for challenge or appeal. Its approach emphasises rigorous legal research, careful examination of the evidentiary record and professional courtroom advocacy, with due regard to the presumption of innocence, procedural safeguards and the right to a fair trial under the laws of Bangladesh.

04.

Cybercrime and Digital Evidence Practice (Cyber & Tech Law)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in criminal proceedings involving allegations of cybercrime, unauthorised access to computer systems, digital fraud, online harassment, electronic communications and other offences under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Cyber Security Ordinance, 2025, as amended or supplemented by applicable law, together with relevant provisions of the Penal Code, 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the Evidence Act, 1872, and other applicable legislation governing digital offences, electronic records and admissibility of evidence.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on analysing the statutory elements of alleged offences, examining digital records and electronic communications, assessing the authenticity and admissibility of electronic evidence, and scrutinising investigative procedures, forensic reports and the attribution of alleged conduct to the accused. The practice encompasses defence submissions, bail applications, challenges to investigative or procedural irregularities where legally maintainable, and trial and appellate proceedings before the competent courts.

05.

Narcotics and Drug Offences Defence Practice (Narcotics & Special Statutes)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in the defence of individuals accused of narcotics-related offences under the laws of Bangladesh, including allegations involving possession, transportation, trafficking and distribution of controlled substances.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Narcotics Control Act, 2018, as amended, together with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the Evidence Act, 1872, the Penal Code, 1860, and other applicable laws and rules governing investigation, search and seizure, evidentiary procedures, trial and punishment.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining the statutory ingredients of alleged offences, scrutinising search, seizure and recovery procedures, assessing the chain of custody and chemical examination reports, and evaluating the admissibility and sufficiency of prosecution evidence. The practice encompasses bail applications, legal challenges to investigative and procedural irregularities where maintainable, defence submissions, witness cross-examination, trial advocacy, and appellate proceedings before the competent courts.

06.

Arms and Explosives Defence Practice (Special Penal Law)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in the defence of individuals accused of offences involving firearms, ammunition, explosives, unlawful possession, use, transportation and related allegations under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Arms Act, 1878, the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, and the Explosives Act, 1884, together with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the Evidence Act, 1872, the Penal Code, 1860, and other applicable laws.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining the statutory ingredients of alleged offences, scrutinising search, seizure and recovery procedures, assessing forensic and ballistic reports, and evaluating the reliability and admissibility of prosecution evidence. The practice encompasses bail applications, challenges to investigative and procedural irregularities where legally maintainable, defence submissions, witness cross-examination, trial advocacy, and appellate proceedings before the competent courts.

07.

Women and Children Criminal Cases (Protective Statutes)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, depending on the client’s engagement, on behalf of complainants and victims as well as accused persons in criminal proceedings involving women and children, including allegations of sexual offences, violence, abduction, trafficking and other offences under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000, the Children Act, 2013, the Penal Code, 1860, and other applicable legislation, together with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 and the Evidence Act, 1872, as relevant to the proceedings.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on analysing the statutory elements of alleged offences, examining complaints and investigation records, assessing witness testimony and documentary or forensic evidence, and evaluating procedural compliance. Depending on the client’s role, representation may include legal advice, bail applications, complaint-related proceedings, witness examination and cross-examination, trial advocacy, and appeals before the competent courts, in accordance with applicable law and fair-trial safeguards.

08.

Special Powers and Public Order Practice (Public Order & Special Statutes)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, depending on the client’s engagement, on behalf of both complainants and accused persons in criminal proceedings involving allegations relating to public order, unlawful activities, preventive detention and offences under special legislation in Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Special Powers Act, 1974, together with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the Penal Code, 1860, and other applicable legislation concerning public order, preventive measures, criminal investigation and trial.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on analysing the statutory basis of the allegations or detention, examining the relevant case records and evidence, assessing compliance with applicable procedural requirements, and identifying legally sustainable grounds for challenge or defence. Depending on the client’s role, representation may include bail applications, challenges to detention orders where maintainable, trial proceedings, legal submissions, and appeals or other remedies before the competent courts.

09.

Human Trafficking and Transnational Crime Practice (Cross-Border & Transnational Crimes)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, depending on the client’s engagement, on behalf of complainants, victims and accused persons in proceedings involving allegations of human trafficking, migrant smuggling, cross-border offences, organised criminal activities and other transnational crimes under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act, 2012, the Overseas Employment and Migrants Act, 2013, and other applicable legislation, together with the Penal Code, 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and relevant laws governing investigation, prosecution and trial.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on analysing the statutory elements of alleged offences, examining witness statements, documentary and financial records, travel and immigration documents, and other relevant evidence. It also involves assessing individual criminal responsibility, the evidentiary basis of alleged participation or conspiracy, and compliance with applicable investigative and procedural requirements. Depending on the client’s role, representation may include complaint-related proceedings, bail applications, defence submissions, witness examination and cross-examination, trial advocacy, and appeals before the competent courts.

10.

Environmental and Regulatory Offences Practice (Regulatory & Environmental Law)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, depending on the client’s engagement, on behalf of complainants, affected parties and accused persons in proceedings involving alleged environmental violations, pollution, unlawful resource use, regulatory non-compliance and other offences under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act, 1995, the Environment Court Act, 2010, and other applicable environmental and regulatory legislation, together with relevant provisions of the Penal Code, 1860, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, where applicable.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on analysing the statutory and regulatory requirements applicable to the alleged conduct, examining inspection reports, environmental assessments, technical evidence and relevant permits or licences, and assessing compliance with enforcement and procedural requirements. Depending on the client’s role, representation may include legal advice, challenges to enforcement measures where maintainable, applications before competent authorities or courts, trial advocacy, and appeals or other remedies available under applicable law.

11.

Criminal Appeals, Revisions and Review Proceedings (Appellate Practice & Supreme Court)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in criminal appellate, revisional and review proceedings before the competent courts and the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, depending on the nature of the case and the client’s engagement.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, and other applicable special legislation and procedural rules governing appeals, revisions, reviews and post-judgment remedies.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining judgments, orders and trial records to identify legally sustainable grounds involving errors of law, misappreciation of evidence, procedural irregularities, jurisdictional issues and sentencing. Depending on the nature of the proceedings, representation may include preparing appeal and revision petitions, applications for leave to appeal, review petitions where legally maintainable, applications for suspension of sentence or bail, and written and oral submissions before the appropriate judicial forums.

12.

Client Counseling & Pre-Trial Legal Consultation (Client Counseling & Pre-Trial Advisory)

Shomaji & Associates provides confidential pre-litigation legal counseling, custodial rights advisory, and pre-trial defense strategy formulation for individuals, corporate executives, and entities facing criminal investigation or prosecution under Bangladeshi law.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The consultation practice is anchored in Articles 27, 31, 32, 33, and 35 of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh (safeguards against arbitrary arrest, custodial protections, and fair trial rights), the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the Evidence Act, 1872 (professional legal privilege), and the Bangladesh Legal Practitioners and Bar Council Canons of Professional Conduct.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our pre-trial consultation approach focuses on immediate risk mitigation, custodial rights enforcement, resisting unlawful remand applications, and advising on anticipatory or regular bail avenues. We guide clients on lawful interactions with law enforcement and regulatory investigating agencies (including the ACC, CID, and DB Police), safeguard attorney-client confidentiality, and structure evidence-based defense strategies prior to formal charge framing.

Chamber Practice Focus & Trial Advocacy

Civil Litigation

Original, Revisional, Appellate & Review Jurisdiction

Civil Litigation & Jurisprudential Scope

Shomaji & Associates provides strategic trial and appellate representation in complex land and property disputes, title and possession, partition, contractual specific performance, money suits, eviction, and civil appeals under the laws of Bangladesh.

Governing Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed principally by the Transfer of Property Act 1882, Registration Act 1908, State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950, Specific Relief Act 1877, Code of Civil Procedure 1908, Premises Rent Control Act 1991, and Arbitration Act 2001.

Chamber Disciplines & Areas of Practice (11)

Comprehensive advisory, statutory frameworks, and courtroom litigation representation across specialized civil litigation areas.

01.

Land and Property Litigation (Property & Real Estate)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in land and property disputes involving ownership, title, possession, inheritance, boundary disputes, unlawful occupation, transfer of property and related civil proceedings under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed by applicable provisions of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the Registration Act, 1908, the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the Specific Relief Act, 1877, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other relevant laws governing land records, property rights, registration and dispute resolution.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining title deeds, chain of ownership, khatian and mutation records, land surveys, possession history and documentary evidence. Depending on the dispute, representation includes title and possession suits, declaration of rights, recovery of possession, injunctions, partition proceedings, challenges to fraudulent transfers or defective documentation, and appeals or revisions before competent courts.

02.

Title, Ownership and Possession Litigation (Title & Possession)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in disputes concerning title, ownership and possession of immovable property, including competing ownership claims, disputed transfers, unlawful occupation, boundary disputes and conflicting land records under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed by the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the Specific Relief Act, 1877, the Registration Act, 1908, the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other applicable laws relating to property rights, land records and civil remedies.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining title deeds, chains of ownership, khatian and mutation records, registration documents, survey reports and evidence of possession. Representation includes suits for declaration of title, recovery of possession, permanent or temporary injunctions, cancellation of instruments where legally maintainable, and appeals or revisions before competent courts.

03.

Partition and Inheritance Related Disputes (Succession & Partition)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in disputes concerning inheritance, succession, partition and distribution of property, including competing claims among heirs, determination of ownership shares, disputed transfers and possession of inherited property under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed by applicable personal laws of succession, including relevant principles of Muslim and Hindu law, together with the Partition Act, 1893, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and other applicable legislation governing property rights and inheritance.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining title documents, inheritance records, deeds of transfer, family relationships, applicable succession rules and the respective shares of the parties. Representation includes partition suits, declaration of shares, recovery of possession, challenges to disputed transfers, interim injunctions and appeals or revisions before competent courts.

04.

Contractual Disputes and Specific Performance (Contracts & Enforcement)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in contractual disputes involving breach of agreement, non-performance of contractual obligations, disputed terms, termination, damages and enforcement of contractual rights under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed principally by the Contract Act, 1872, the Specific Relief Act, 1877, and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, together with other applicable legislation governing contractual obligations, remedies and enforcement.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining contractual terms, the validity and enforceability of agreements, performance and breach of obligations, and available legal remedies. Representation includes claims for specific performance, compensation or damages, declarations of contractual rights, injunctions, contractual defences and appeals before competent courts.

05.

Money Suits and Debt Recovery (Commercial & Financial Recovery)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation for both creditors and debtors in disputes involving outstanding debts, unpaid contractual dues, loans, advances, financial obligations and recovery claims under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed principally by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the Contract Act, 1872, Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, for matters within its statutory scope.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining loan agreements, contractual documents, financial statements, payment records and evidence of alleged liability or repayment. Representation includes filing or defending money suits, debt recovery proceedings, claims involving dishonoured payment instruments, execution of decrees, applications for interim relief, and appeals or revisions.

06.

Injunctions and Declaratory Relief (Civil Injunctions & Relief)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in proceedings seeking or opposing injunctions and declaratory relief concerning property rights, contractual obligations, ownership, possession and other civil disputes under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed principally by the Specific Relief Act, 1877, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other applicable legislation governing civil remedies, interim protection and enforcement of legal rights.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining legal rights asserted by parties, factual and documentary basis of claims, and statutory requirements for interim or permanent relief. Representation includes applications for temporary, perpetual or mandatory injunctions, suits for declaration of legal rights, challenges to injunction applications, and appeals or revisions.

07.

Lease, Tenancy and Eviction (Tenancy & Rent Control)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation to landlords, tenants, lessors and lessees in disputes involving lease agreements, tenancy rights, rent arrears, termination of tenancy, recovery of possession and eviction under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed principally by the Premises Rent Control Act, 1991, the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the Registration Act, 1908, and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, together with other applicable tenancy legislation.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining lease agreements, rent receipts, notices of termination, payment records and legal grounds for possession or eviction. Representation includes eviction proceedings, defences against eviction claims, recovery of rent or possession, disputes concerning lease termination, and appeals before competent courts.

08.

Deed, Registration and Documentation Disputes (Deeds & Instruments)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in disputes involving deeds, property transfers, registration, forged or disputed documents, defective instruments and the legal validity or enforceability of documentary transactions under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed principally by the Registration Act, 1908, the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the Specific Relief Act, 1877, the Evidence Act, 1872, and other applicable legislation governing deeds, registration, documentary evidence and property transactions.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining authenticity, execution, registration and legal effect of disputed instruments, together with title records and evidence of parties' intentions. Representation includes suits for declaration, cancellation of instruments where legally maintainable, challenges to disputed transfers, claims involving forgery or misrepresentation, and related civil proceedings.

09.

Arbitration (Dispute Resolution)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in domestic and international arbitration and related dispute resolution proceedings involving contractual, commercial, construction and other civil disputes.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed principally by the Arbitration Act, 2001, together with applicable contractual provisions, arbitration rules and other relevant laws governing arbitral proceedings, enforcement of arbitral awards and judicial intervention.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on analysing arbitration agreements, assessing the scope of arbitral jurisdiction, preparing claims and defences, presenting documentary and oral evidence, and addressing procedural issues. Representation includes arbitration proceedings, applications for interim measures, challenges to arbitral awards, and applications for recognition and enforcement.

10.

Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) (Mediation & Settlement)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal assistance and representation in alternative dispute resolution processes, including mediation, negotiation, conciliation and court-referred settlement of civil, commercial, contractual and property disputes.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed by applicable provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including sections 89A, 89B and 89C, where applicable, together with relevant provisions of the Arbitration Act, 2001, and other legislation governing settlement and dispute resolution.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on identifying legal and factual issues in dispute, assessing respective rights and obligations, and facilitating legally sound and mutually acceptable settlements. Assistance includes settlement negotiations, mediation, preparation and review of settlement agreements, court-referred ADR proceedings, and steps to record or enforce settlements.

11.

Civil Appeals, Revisions and Execution Proceedings (Appellate & Execution)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in civil appellate, revisional and execution proceedings involving property disputes, contractual claims, money suits, declaratory relief and other civil matters before the competent courts of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Governed principally by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including its provisions relating to appeals, revisions and execution of decrees, together with the Limitation Act, 1908, and other applicable procedural rules.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining judgments, decrees, orders and trial records to identify legally sustainable grounds for appeal or revision, assess procedural irregularities, and determine remedies under the law. Execution practice includes applications for enforcement of decrees, recovery of decretal amounts, delivery of possession, defending execution proceedings, and interim relief.

Corporate Law

Corporate Governance, Financial Crimes, Banking Recovery & Commercial Arbitration

Corporate Law & Jurisprudential Scope

Comprehensive legal representation in financial crimes, Negotiable Instruments (NI Act Sec 138), Artha Rin Adalat, corporate governance, commercial arbitration, M&A restructuring, and banking credit disputes.

Governing Statutory & Legal Framework: Practice governed by Companies Act 1994, Bank Companies Act 1991, Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003, Arbitration Act 2001, Negotiable Instruments Act 1881, BSEC Act 1993, and Contract Act 1872.

Chamber Disciplines & Areas of Practice (15)

Comprehensive advisory, statutory frameworks, and courtroom litigation representation across specialized corporate law areas.

01.

Financial Crimes Practice (Financial Crimes)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in criminal proceedings involving allegations of financial fraud, embezzlement, forgery, fraudulent transactions, money laundering, misappropriation of funds and other financial offences under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed by applicable provisions of the Penal Code, 1860, the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and other relevant legislation governing financial offences, investigation, prosecution and trial.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on examining financial transactions, banking records, contractual documents, audit reports and other documentary evidence to assess the statutory elements of alleged offences, the evidentiary basis of criminal liability and compliance with investigative procedures. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include bail applications, defence submissions, challenges to proceedings where legally maintainable, witness examination and cross-examination, trial advocacy, and appellate proceedings before the competent courts.

02.

Commercial Criminal Litigation (Commercial Litigation)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in criminal proceedings arising from commercial and corporate transactions, including allegations of fraud, criminal breach of trust, forgery, falsification of accounts, misappropriation of funds, cheque dishonour and other business-related offences under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice encompasses applicable provisions of the Penal Code, 1860, the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, the Companies Act, 1994, and other relevant legislation governing commercial transactions, corporate conduct, financial offences and criminal liability.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on analysing the legal elements of alleged offences, examining contractual obligations and commercial representations, scrutinising banking records, corporate documents and financial transactions, and assessing the distinction between civil or contractual liability and criminal culpability. Particular attention is given to the attribution of liability to directors, officers and other individuals, the evidentiary basis of allegations of fraud or dishonest intention, and compliance with applicable investigation and procedural requirements. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include complaint and defence proceedings, bail applications, challenges to proceedings where legally maintainable, evidentiary submissions, trial advocacy, and appellate or revisional proceedings before the competent courts.

03.

Negotiable Instruments Practice (NI Act Section 138) (Banking & Debt Recovery)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in disputes and proceedings involving negotiable instruments, including cheques, promissory notes, bills of exchange and other instruments recognised under applicable law. The practice encompasses disputes concerning dishonour, payment obligations, validity, enforceability, transfer, endorsement, negotiation and liability arising from such instruments.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, together with applicable provisions of the Contract Act, 1872, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and other relevant laws, depending on the nature of the dispute and the remedy sought.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining the legal character, execution, validity and enforceability of the instrument; the rights and liabilities of the parties; consideration and underlying payment obligations; endorsement, transfer and negotiation; presentment and dishonour, where applicable; statutory notice and limitation requirements; and the admissibility and probative value of documentary and banking evidence. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include pursuing or defending claims and complaints, challenging liability and maintainability, examining witnesses, addressing procedural and evidentiary issues, seeking appropriate civil or criminal remedies where legally available, and conducting trial, appellate and revisional proceedings before the competent courts.

04.

Artha Rin Adalat Litigation (Banking & Debt Recovery)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in proceedings before the Artha Rin Adalat concerning the recovery of institutional loans and financial liabilities. The practice includes representing financial institutions and lenders pursuing recovery claims, as well as borrowers, guarantors and other defendants responding to such claims under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, together with relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the Contract Act, 1872, the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and other applicable laws, depending on the nature of the claim, security and proceedings.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining loan and financing agreements, sanction letters, statements of account, repayment records, security documents, mortgages, guarantees and other relevant evidence. Particular attention is given to the calculation and enforceability of the claimed debt, compliance with applicable legal and procedural requirements, the respective liabilities of borrowers and guarantors, and claims concerning secured assets. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include instituting or defending recovery suits, contesting claims and calculations, addressing interim applications, participating in court proceedings, pursuing appeals or other remedies where legally maintainable, and assisting with execution of decrees.

05.

Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) (Arbitration & ADR)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal assistance in resolving disputes through alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms, including mediation, negotiation, conciliation and arbitration. Depending on the client’s engagement and the nature of the dispute, the practice covers civil, commercial, contractual, family, employment and other matters suitable for settlement under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The applicable legal framework includes the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (sections 89A, 89B and 89C); the Arbitration Act, 2001; the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (sections 22–25); the Family Courts Act, 2023 (sections 11 and 15); the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 (sections 209, 210 and 213); the Legal Aid Services Act, 2000 (section 21A(2)); and section 345 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, concerning the compounding of legally compoundable offences, where applicable.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach focuses on identifying the central issues, assessing the parties’ legal rights and obligations, evaluating potential risks and remedies, and exploring practical settlement options. Depending on the circumstances, assistance may include negotiation with opposing parties, participation in mediation or conciliation, arbitration-related proceedings, preparation and review of settlement terms, court-referred ADR, and advice on recording, implementing or enforcing settlements in accordance with applicable law. Where settlement is not feasible or appropriate, we advise on available legal remedies and the continuation of proceedings before the competent court or forum.

06.

Arbitration Practice (Arbitration & ADR)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal assistance and representation in arbitration proceedings involving commercial, contractual, construction, investment-related and other disputes where arbitration is available under the applicable law or agreement. Depending on the client’s engagement, the practice includes representing claimants and respondents in domestic arbitration, as well as advising on arbitration agreements, arbitral proceedings and the legal remedies available before the competent courts of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Arbitration Act, 2001, together with relevant provisions of the Contract Act, 1872, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other applicable laws. The legal framework may also include the New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards, 1958, where relevant to the recognition and enforcement of foreign arbitral awards in Bangladesh.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining arbitration agreements, contractual obligations, the nature of the dispute, jurisdictional objections, applicable procedural rules and the evidence supporting each party’s position. Depending on the client’s interests, assistance may include drafting and reviewing arbitration clauses, preparing statements of claim and defence, presenting documentary and witness evidence, addressing jurisdictional and interim issues, participating in hearings, and pursuing challenges to or enforcement of arbitral awards where legally permissible under applicable law.

07.

Corporate Governance & Compliance Disputes (Corporate Governance & Compliance)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal advice and representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in disputes involving corporate governance, directors’ and officers’ duties, shareholder rights, board decisions, regulatory compliance and internal corporate affairs. The practice encompasses disputes arising from alleged breaches of statutory or fiduciary duties, irregular corporate resolutions, conflicts of interest, mismanagement, disclosure obligations and disagreements concerning corporate control and decision-making under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Companies Act, 1994, together with applicable provisions of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969, the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission Act, 1993, relevant securities regulations and rules, and other legislation applicable to the company’s legal status, industry and regulatory obligations.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining corporate documents, articles of association, board and shareholder resolutions, minutes of meetings, statutory filings, financial statements, audit reports and relevant regulatory correspondence. Particular attention is given to directors’ and officers’ individual responsibilities, compliance with statutory and constitutional requirements, shareholder rights, conflicts of interest, decision-making authority and the distinction between corporate liability and personal liability. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include pursuing or defending corporate claims, challenging resolutions or transactions where legally maintainable, addressing regulatory proceedings, seeking appropriate interim relief, and conducting litigation, appeals or other proceedings before competent courts and regulatory forums.

08.

Contracts & Commercial Transactions Disputes (Commercial Litigation)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal advice and representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in disputes arising from contractual obligations, commercial transactions and business arrangements. The practice covers disagreements concerning contractual interpretation, breach of contract, non-performance, payment obligations, misrepresentation, termination, indemnities, guarantees and the validity or enforceability of contractual terms and transactions under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Contract Act, 1872, together with the Specific Relief Act, 1877, the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the Registration Act, 1908, the Evidence Act, 1872, and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, where applicable. Depending on the nature of the transaction and the parties involved, other legislation may also apply, including the Companies Act, 1994, the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, the Arbitration Act, 2001, and relevant consumer protection or sector-specific laws.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining contractual documents, transaction records, correspondence, payment histories, performance obligations and supporting evidence to assess the parties’ respective rights and liabilities. Particular attention is given to contractual interpretation, breach and causation, enforceability, available remedies, limitation periods and the distinction between civil contractual liability and conduct that may give rise to separate legal consequences. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include pursuing or defending claims for damages, compensation, specific performance, declarations or injunctions where legally available, negotiating settlements, and conducting proceedings before the competent courts or arbitral tribunals.

09.

Mergers, Acquisitions & Corporate Restructuring Disputes (Corporate Governance & Compliance)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal advice and representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in disputes arising from mergers, acquisitions, business transfers, corporate reorganisations, amalgamations and restructuring transactions. The practice covers disagreements concerning transaction agreements, shareholder rights, corporate approvals, valuation, representations and warranties, disclosure obligations, contractual performance, regulatory compliance and the legal consequences of changes in corporate ownership or control under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The applicable legal framework includes the Companies Act, 1994, the Contract Act, 1872, the Competition Act, 2012, the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969, the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission Act, 1993, and relevant rules and regulations governing securities and capital-market transactions. Depending on the nature of the transaction, the parties involved and the relief sought, the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the Registration Act, 1908, the Arbitration Act, 2001, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other applicable laws may also be relevant.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining transaction documents, share purchase agreements, merger or amalgamation schemes, board and shareholder resolutions, due diligence materials, financial statements, valuation reports, regulatory filings and related correspondence. Particular attention is given to compliance with statutory approval requirements, contractual obligations, representations and warranties, shareholder and creditor interests, disclosure issues and potential director or officer liability. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include pursuing or defending claims arising from disputed transactions, challenging corporate decisions where legally maintainable, seeking declarations or interim relief, addressing regulatory proceedings, and pursuing arbitration, litigation or appellate remedies before the competent courts and forums.

10.

Shareholder and Directors’ Disputes (Corporate Governance & Compliance)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal advice and representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in disputes involving shareholders, directors and corporate management. The practice covers disagreements concerning shareholder rights, board decisions, voting rights, dividend entitlements, corporate control, alleged breaches of directors’ duties, conflicts of interest, mismanagement, access to corporate records and the validity of corporate resolutions under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The practice is governed principally by the Companies Act, 1994, together with the Contract Act, 1872, the Specific Relief Act, 1877, the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969, the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission Act, 1993, and applicable securities rules and regulations. Depending on the nature of the dispute, the company’s status and the relief sought, the Arbitration Act, 2001, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and other relevant legislation may also apply.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining the company’s memorandum and articles of association, shareholders’ agreements, board and general meeting resolutions, minutes, statutory registers, financial statements and relevant correspondence. Particular attention is given to the allocation of decision-making authority, compliance with statutory and constitutional requirements, directors’ duties, potential conflicts of interest, the distinction between corporate and personal liability, and the legal remedies available to affected parties. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include pursuing or defending shareholder and director claims, challenging resolutions or transactions where legally maintainable, seeking declarations or injunctive relief, addressing regulatory issues, and conducting arbitration, litigation or appellate proceedings before the competent forums.

11.

Foreign Investment and Joint Venture Disputes (Foreign Investment & Capital Markets)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal advice and representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in disputes arising from foreign investment, joint ventures, cross-border commercial arrangements and foreign participation in business operations in Bangladesh. The practice covers disagreements concerning joint venture agreements, shareholders’ rights, capital contributions, profit distribution, management and control, contractual obligations, transfer of shares, exit arrangements, repatriation of investment proceeds and alleged breaches of investment-related agreements or regulatory requirements.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The applicable legal framework includes the Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1980, the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority Act, 2016, the Companies Act, 1994, the Contract Act, 1872, the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947, and the Arbitration Act, 2001. Depending on the nature of the investment and dispute, relevant provisions of the Competition Act, 2012, the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the Registration Act, 1908, applicable foreign exchange regulations and investment-related rules may also apply.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining investment agreements, joint venture contracts, shareholders’ agreements, corporate records, capital contribution documents, financial statements, regulatory approvals and cross-border transaction records. Particular attention is given to contractual obligations, ownership and control rights, regulatory compliance, dispute resolution clauses, jurisdiction, governing law and the enforceability of contractual or arbitral remedies. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include pursuing or defending contractual claims, addressing shareholder and management disputes, participating in arbitration, seeking interim or injunctive relief where legally available, and pursuing recognition or enforcement of arbitral awards or other remedies before competent courts and forums.

12.

Securities and Capital Market Regulation Disputes (Foreign Investment & Capital Markets)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal advice and representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in disputes involving securities transactions, capital-market activities, regulatory compliance and enforcement proceedings in Bangladesh. The practice covers matters concerning listed companies, investors, directors, sponsors, intermediaries and other market participants, including allegations of securities-law violations, disclosure failures, market manipulation, insider trading, irregular share transactions and breaches of regulatory requirements.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The applicable legal framework includes the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission Act, 1993, the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969, the Companies Act, 1994, the Securities and Exchange Rules, 2020, and applicable rules, regulations, directives and orders issued by the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission. Depending on the nature of the dispute, relevant provisions of the Financial Reporting Act, 2015, the Contract Act, 1872, the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and other applicable legislation may also be relevant.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining regulatory notices, investigation reports, trading records, disclosure documents, financial statements, audit reports, corporate resolutions and relevant correspondence. Particular attention is given to the statutory basis of regulatory action, compliance with disclosure and reporting obligations, the sufficiency of supporting evidence, procedural fairness and the potential liability of companies, directors, officers and other market participants. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include responding to regulatory inquiries, pursuing or defending enforcement proceedings, challenging regulatory decisions where legally maintainable, addressing investor and transaction-related disputes, and conducting litigation, appeals or other proceedings before competent courts and regulatory forums.

13.

Insolvency, Winding-Up and Liquidation Disputes (Banking & Debt Recovery)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal advice and representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in disputes concerning corporate insolvency, winding-up, liquidation and the settlement of outstanding liabilities. The practice covers matters involving companies, creditors, shareholders, directors, secured lenders and other stakeholders, including disputes over unpaid debts, inability to meet financial obligations, winding-up petitions, claims against company assets, creditor priorities, directors’ responsibilities and the distribution of assets during liquidation.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The applicable legal framework includes the Companies Act, 1994, particularly its provisions concerning winding-up and liquidation, the Bankruptcy Act, 1997, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the Contract Act, 1872, and other relevant laws governing debt recovery, security interests and corporate liabilities. Depending on the nature of the proceedings and the parties involved, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and applicable regulatory requirements may also be relevant.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining financial statements, loan agreements, creditor claims, security documents, corporate records, statutory notices and evidence concerning the company’s financial position. Particular attention is given to the legal grounds for winding-up, the validity and priority of creditor claims, the treatment of secured and unsecured liabilities, compliance with statutory procedures, and the potential liabilities of directors or other responsible persons. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include filing or opposing winding-up petitions, pursuing or defending creditor claims, challenging disputed liabilities, addressing liquidation-related proceedings, and pursuing appeals or other remedies before the competent courts and forums.

14.

Banking Matters & Credit Facilities Disputes (Banking & Debt Recovery)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal advice and representation, depending on the client’s engagement, in banking-related disputes and proceedings involving financial institutions, borrowers, guarantors, directors, corporate entities and other stakeholders. The practice covers disputes concerning loan facilities, credit transactions, loan recovery, default classification, security and guarantees, banking documentation, alleged financial irregularities, regulatory compliance and the rights and obligations arising from banking relationships under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The applicable legal framework includes the Bank Companies Act, 1991, the Bangladesh Bank Order, 1972, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the Contract Act, 1872, the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, the Bankruptcy Act, 1997, and the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, where relevant. Depending on the nature of the dispute, applicable Bangladesh Bank circulars, prudential regulations, foreign exchange regulations and other relevant banking and financial legislation may also apply.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining loan and facility agreements, sanction letters, statements of account, security documents, guarantees, mortgage instruments, banking correspondence, regulatory notices and relevant financial records. Particular attention is given to the contractual and statutory basis of the claim, the calculation of outstanding liabilities, the classification of loans, compliance with applicable banking regulations, the enforceability of securities and guarantees, and the distinction between corporate obligations and the personal liability of directors or other individuals. Depending on the client’s position, representation may include pursuing or defending recovery proceedings, challenging disputed liabilities or regulatory decisions where legally maintainable, addressing banking and financial disputes, seeking appropriate interim relief, and conducting litigation, appeals or other proceedings before competent courts and regulatory forums.

15.

Client Counseling & Corporate Strategic Advisory (Strategic Advisory)

Shomaji & Associates provides confidential pre-litigation counseling, corporate compliance audits, board fiduciary advisory, and risk-mitigation strategies for domestic and multinational commercial enterprises operating in Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Companies Act 1994, Bangladesh Bank Regulations, BSEC Directives, Contract Act 1872, and standard ADR and professional legal privilege standards.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: We assist corporate leadership with early-stage risk assessments, contractual dispute pre-emption, internal governance reviews, regulatory negotiation, and preparation for contentious court or arbitration proceedings.

Chamber Practice Focus & Trial Advocacy

Family Matter

Matrimonial Disputes, Child Custody & Shariah Advisory

Family Matter & Jurisprudential Scope

Compassionate and rigorous advocacy in marriage, divorce, dower (denmohor), maintenance, child custody, guardianship, dowry defense, and Muslim family law.

Governing Statutory & Legal Framework: Practice grounded in Family Courts Act 2023, Guardians and Wards Act 1890, Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, Dowry Prohibition Act 2018, Domestic Violence Act 2010, and classical Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh).

Chamber Disciplines & Areas of Practice (13)

Comprehensive advisory, statutory frameworks, and courtroom litigation representation across specialized family matter areas.

01.

Marriage and Matrimonial Disputes (Matrimonial Law)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal advice and representation in disputes concerning marriage, marital status, validity of marriage, registration formalities and the rights and obligations arising from matrimonial relationships under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The applicable legal framework includes the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Act 1974, the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1937, Special Marriage Act 1872, and Family Courts Act 2023.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining marriage registration records, marriage contracts, relevant documents, and other evidence to assess the legal status of the marriage and enforce respective rights.

02.

Divorce and Dissolution of Marriage (Matrimonial Law)

Legal advice and representation in matters concerning divorce, dissolution of marriage and the legal consequences of marital separation under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The applicable legal framework includes the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act 1939, Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Act 1974, and Family Courts Act 2023.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Our approach involves examining divorce notices, marriage documents, registration records, statutory timelines, and consequences for dower, maintenance, and child custody.

03.

Dower (Denmohor) and Maintenance (Financial Rights)

Legal advice and representation in disputes concerning dower (denmohor), spousal maintenance and related financial obligations arising from marriage or its dissolution under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: The applicable legal framework includes the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1937, and the Family Courts Act 2023.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Examining kabinnama (marriage contract), payment proofs, financial capacity, prompt and deferred dower terms, and decree execution.

04.

Restitution of Conjugal Rights (Matrimonial Law)

Representation in proceedings concerning restitution of conjugal rights under the applicable personal laws of Bangladesh when one spouse withdraws without lawful justification.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Family Courts Act 2023, Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1937, and relevant personal and family laws.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Examining marriage documents, cohabitation evidence, and legally recognized grounds for seeking or resisting relief.

05.

Child Custody, Guardianship and Visitation (Child Welfare & Custody)

Disputes concerning child custody, legal guardianship, visitation schedules and parental access under the laws of Bangladesh, prioritizing the child’s welfare and best interests.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Guardians and Wards Act 1890, Family Courts Act 2023, Children Act 2013, and applicable personal law rules.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Prioritizing child welfare, physical, moral, and emotional development, and securing workable visitation and custody decrees.

06.

Matrimonial Property Disputes (Property & Inheritance)

Disputes concerning ownership, possession, transfer and recovery of property arising from matrimonial relationships under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Transfer of Property Act 1882, Specific Relief Act 1877, Registration Act 1908, CPC 1908, and Family Courts Act 2023.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Examining title deeds, financial records, bank statements, evidence of contribution, and securing interim protective injunctions.

07.

Succession Certificates and Legal Heirship (Property & Inheritance)

Matters concerning succession certificates, legal heirship identification, inheritance rights and the administration of estates under the laws of Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Succession Act 1925, Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1937, CPC 1908, and personal succession laws.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Reviewing family genealogies, death records, bank deposits and securities, and filing succession petitions before competent courts.

08.

Dowry-Related Criminal Cases (Criminal & Protection)

Representation in criminal proceedings involving allegations of dowry-related demands, harassment, coercion, and related offences under matrimonial relationships.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Dowry Prohibition Act 2018, Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000, Penal Code 1860, and CrPC 1898.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Examining complaints, First Information Reports (FIR), medical documentation, communications, and securing bail or conducting robust defense.

09.

Domestic Violence and Protection (Criminal & Protection)

Matters involving domestic violence, applications for emergency protection orders, residence orders, and related family or criminal proceedings.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act 2010, Domestic Violence Rules 2013, and Family Courts Act 2023.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Filing urgent protection applications, securing safe residence orders, medical report verification, and defending against unsubstantiated allegations.

10.

Adoption and Child Welfare (Child Welfare & Custody)

Matters concerning child welfare, guardianship, foster care arrangements and legal procedures applicable to child protection in Bangladesh.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Guardians and Wards Act 1890, Family Courts Act 2023, Children Act 2013, and Child Marriage Restraint Act 2017.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Assisting prospective guardians, executing guardianship petitions, verifying parentage and child protection clearances.

11.

Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) (ADR & Mediation)

Alternative dispute resolution (ADR) in family disputes focusing on negotiation, mediation, and amicable reconciliation with due regard to legal rights.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Family Courts Act 2023 (mandatory pre-trial and post-trial reconciliation), Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, and principles of Sulh.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Facilitating private mediation, drafting enforceable compromise deeds (solenama), and concluding disputes with dignity.

12.

Muslim Family Law and Shariah Advisory (Shariah Advisory)

Advisory and representation concerning Muslim family law, Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh) and Shariah principles in Bangladesh across Nikah, Talaq, Mahr, Nafaqah, and Mirath (Fara’id).

Statutory & Legal Framework: The Qur’an, Sunnah, established Madhahib jurisprudence, MFLO 1961, and Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1937.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Issuing comprehensive legal opinions, calculating exact Shariah inheritance shares (Fara’id), and representing clients before family tribunals.

13.

Client Counseling (Advisory & Consultation)

Confidential, sensitive client counseling on family rights, divorce options, custody risks, and pre-litigation resolution.

Statutory & Legal Framework: Family Courts Act 2023 and legal ethics codes.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach: Compassionate, objective assessment of domestic legal rights and dispute settlement avenues.
